Cob accepted two silver crowns from Bartholomew and tucked them away.
Sir Bartholomew successfully climbed the hoist rope and reached the beam beside Prout.
From beside the body, Sir Bartholomew saw a second, narrow level mark on Prout’s neck beneath the noose mark, swelling beneath the hair at the back of his head, and clean palms.
Cob accepted two silver crowns from Sir Bartholomew and said he found the boots in the yard; he kept the boots on.
Kell recorded the two-crown payment and Cob’s answer in her notebook.
